Because this is a reporting factsheet rather than an author-led microdata ML analysis, the manuscript does not document whether analysts applied specific weight variables directly in a custom workflow.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Mongolia factsheet summarises how 15-year-old students in Mongolia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how performance relates to student and school experiences. Mongolia participated for the first time in PISA in 2022, with 6 999 students in 195 schools completing the assessment in one of the three domains. The factsheet reports mean performance comparisons with the OECD average and selected comparison countries, as well as proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2+ and Level 5/6) with 95% confidence intervals. It also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and describes aspects of school climate, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. No author-led predictive modelling is conducted in this factsheet; therefore, there are no ML model metrics, PV-handling details, or missing-data procedures documented beyond OECD’s standard PISA reporting.
